title: Film Extrusion of Crambe abyssinica/Wheat Gluten Blends
protocol: Sieve the crambe meal with a round, fine-mesh stainless steel kitchen sieve (pore size: ~1.5 mm, 14 mesh) to remove large fiber fractions and uncrushed seeds.
Store the sieved meal at -18°C to prevent material ageing.
Mill the sieved crambe meal in a rotary ball mill with ceramic balls using a 53 rpm jar revolution rate for 24 hours.
Condition all the ball-milled crambe meal and wheat gluten powder in open jars for a minimum of 48 hours at 23°C and a relative humidity of 50%.
Grind urea powder to fine particles with a mortar and pestle.
Blend urea and glycerol (25.5 g of glycerol and 15 g of urea per 100 g of the final mixture).
Heat the glycerol to 65°C in a glass flask in an oil bath.
Add the urea powder slowly to the heated glycerol.
Stir the mixture with a magnetic stirrer at 65°C until the urea powder is completely dissolved.
Blend crambe meal powder and wheat gluten powder in a kitchen mixing machine for 5 min.
Slowly add the glycerol/urea mixture to the crambe/wheat gluten blend in the kitchen mixing machine while stirring the mixture.
Continue mixing for approximately 2 min until a homogeneous dough is obtained.
Prepare 500 g of the mixture each time, using specific relative contents of constituents as described.
Set zones 1-10 along the extruder barrel at a low temperature profile: 75-75-75-80-80-80-80-85-85-85 °C to perform film extrusion in a twin-screw extruder.
Use a flat sheet die (45 mm x 0.7 mm) for extruding films.
Choose a screw speed between 30 rpm and 200 rpm, recording the die pressure during extrusion.
Feed the dough manually through the hopper with a wooden pusher.
Support material flow towards the screws with the wooden pusher.
Pick up the extrudate at the die with a conveyor belt operating at 2.0 m/min.
Place air ventilation cooling (fans) along the conveyor belt.
Run different die temperatures (105 °C-(105 °C), 110 °C-(110 °C), 125 °C-(115 °C), 130 °C-(120 °C), and 140 °C-(125 °C)) to select conditions for the smoothest extrudate with minimum voids.
Adjust temperature in zone 11 next to the die as indicated.
Store extrudates in sealed polyethylene bags after extrusion.
Extrude films using a high-temperature profile (85-85-85-100-100-100-110-110-120-120-120 °C for zones 1 to 11).
Use die temperatures of 125 °C and 130 °C for film extrusion.
Extrude material as continuous strands in the extruder using a two-strand die to get pellets.
Use low-T profile for the extruder barrel.
Set screw rotational speed at 60 rpm.
Use different die-(zone 11) temperatures (130 °C, 125 °C, 105 °C, and 85 °C) to obtain strands with the smoothest surfaces.
Feed the strands into a pelletizer operated at a cutting speed of 7 m/min after passing through the conveyor belt.
Feed pellets manually into the extruder and extrude films with low-T profile inside the barrel and die temperature of 125 °C, using a screw rotational speed of 30 rpm.
Use pellets previously extruded at 85 °C for automatic feeding simulation.
Connect the feeder to the extruder in volumetric feeder mode with a feeding volume of 35 kg/h and hopper and extruder screw speeds of 16 and 120 rpm, respectively.
Extrude using low temperature profile barrel and die-(zone 11) temperature of 125 °C.
Cut two extrudates into pieces of 4.4 cm x 7.0 cm and 2.6 cm x 7.0 cm for the first setup.
Place cut pieces next to each other in an aluminum rectangular frame (70 x 70 x 0.5 mm³).
Sandwich the frame between two aluminum plates using PET films on both sides to prevent adhesion.
Place them into the press.
Set the pressure gauge on the press to 200 or 400 bar.
Press the films with a plate temperature of 110, 120, and 130 °C for 10 and 20 min.
Cut out rectangular samples (4.4 cm x 4.4 cm) from unextruded material.
Sandwich the samples between two aluminum plates using PET films on both sides to prevent adhesion.
Place them into the press.
Set the pressure gauge to 50 bar, 75 bar, or 100 bar.
Press the films for 5 or 10 min at plate temperatures of 110 °C, 120 °C and 130 °C.
